what: The Average Calculator finds the mean, median, mode, range, sum, count, smallest and largest value of any list of numbers, plus the geometric and harmonic means when all numbers are positive. Switch to weighted mode when some values count more than others, such as course grades.
A second tab handles ratios: simplify a ratio (even with decimals), solve a proportion like 3 : 4 = 15 : ?, and share an amount in a ratio such as 2 : 3 : 5.
uses: Average test scores or work out a weighted course grade.
Find the average spend per week.
Get the median and range of measurements.
Scale a ratio up or down.
Split profits or costs in a ratio.
tutorial: Type or paste numbers separated by commas, spaces or new lines. Press "Try an example" to see how it works.
For weighted averages, type one value and its weight per line, like 85 30.
Mean, median, mode, range and more appear as you type.
Open the Ratio tab and type a ratio like 12:18 to get 2 : 3.
Fill in three of the four boxes and leave the unknown one empty.
Type the amount and the ratio to see each part.
features: Mean, median, mode, weighted, geometric and harmonic.
Paste thousands of numbers from a spreadsheet.
Shows every mode, or says when there is none.
Copy all the figures in one click.

example.title: Worked example: weighted grade
example.text: Coursework 85% is worth 30%, a project 72% is worth 20% and the exam 90% is worth 50%. In weighted mode type 85 30, 72 20 and 90 50 on three lines. The weighted average is (85×30 + 72×20 + 90×50) ÷ 100 = 84.9%, while the simple average would be 82.3%.

tips: Use a dot for decimals; commas separate numbers.
The median is better than the mean when a few values are extreme.
Weights do not have to add up to 100.
In ratios, order matters: 2 : 3 is not 3 : 2.
problems: It says something is not a number
Remove units, currency symbols or thousands separators like 1,000.
Weighted mode says a line needs a weight
Each line needs exactly two numbers: the value and its weight.
Use colons between parts and only positive numbers.
